verdict.rationale: LanceDB documents filtering query results on metadata fields and pre-filtering, where the `where(...)` condition runs before vector search so only matching rows are considered. That design protects recall. A community comment corroborates predicate pushdown for filtering. The latency half of the story is not documented. missing for 10: evidence of latency behaviour under filters (scalar/metadata indexes, benchmarks), documented recall guarantees with ANN indexes plus filters, examples of complex structured filter conditions on vector search.

support.subject: As a developer, I can filter vector search by structured metadata conditions without wrecking recall or latency

citations.quote: LanceDB supports filtering features of query results based on metadata fields.
Pre-filtering means LanceDB applies the metadata `where(...)` condition before running vector search, so the search only considers rows that already match the filter.
They do predicate pushdown for filtering too.
